name: Nimo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A40.1 (hdl 1885/254341).
sources.note: p.10, Figure C 'Summary of Arai Phonology' (verified on page scan): gives seven contrasting vowels for Nimo, then 'Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga' with Ama minimal pairs. Nimo is NOT named among the languages with (contrastive) stress; nothing on where stress falls in Nimo. Table 2 Nimo wordlist column (pp.20-24) carries no stress marks (checked p.21 image).

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Nimo' (wordlist from Conrad & Dye 1975 and SIL 1963).
sources.note: Lexical forms only; no phonological notes.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. [uploaded 2010]. Nimo Swadesh List (archive.org item rosettaproject_niw_swadesh-1; source of forms not stated).
sources.note: 346 gloss:form lines in two transcriptions; no stress marks anywhere; no prose.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 243-273. DOI 10.15144/PL-A76.243.
sources.note: No Nimo data at all (survey of other Upper Sepik languages); silent on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. Sko, Kwomtari, and Left May (Arai) phyla. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 849-858. Canberra: ANU (hdl 1885/252979).
sources.note: p.855 lists 'Nimo (Nimo-Wasuai, Nakwi) 413' and says 'Insufficient data is available on the typological features of the group, although Conrad and Dye give an outline of phonological features'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU (hdl 1885/146478).
sources.note: Entry 168 NIMO-WASUAI (Birua): villages listed; 'SIL word lists and Basel list from Aimi identify this language, but no further details are available.' Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages nimo1247 (Nimo), nimo1248 (Nimo-Nakwi), left1242 (Left May).
sources.note: 0 descriptive references for Nimo; only Conrad & Dye 1975, Laycock 1973/1975, Ethnologue. Family-level refs add only Årsjö 1999 (Ama). Nothing on stress.
Classification, villages, speaker count only; no phonology.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: The only modern handbook treatment of the Left May family; its phonology paragraph for Left May may generalise (or explicitly decline to generalise) stress facts beyond Ama and would be the citable modern statement if it mentions Nimo.
